docs.title: Odoo Operator
docs.text:
The Odoo Operator runs Odoo on Kubernetes. You describe an instance in one OdooDeployment, and the operator does the rest:

  • it creates or adopts the PostgreSQL database;
  • it installs the modules you list, in a Job, before Odoo starts;
  • it renders odoo.conf from the spec;
  • it runs the Deployment, Services and filestore volume;
  • it upgrades the database when the image changes, or when you ask it to;
  • it serves a maintenance page while Odoo is installed, upgraded or started;
  • it backs up the database and filestore to S3, SFTP, NFS or a volume, and restores them in place, with an undo.

docs.text:

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This page takes you from an empty cluster to Odoo open in your browser and a first backup, in about fifteen minutes. It uses the repository's samples, which bring their own PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
• A Kubernetes cluster, 1.28 or newer, and kubectl with cluster-admin rights (the install creates CRDs and cluster roles).
  • A default StorageClass. The sample asks for storageClassName: standard; if your cluster has no class of that name, change spec.odooFilestore.storageClassName in config/samples/odoo_v1_odoodeployment.yaml.

  • A clone of the repository, for the samples:

    git clone https://github.com/MohanadAbugharbia/odoo-operator.git
cd odoo-operator

docs.title: 1. Install the operator
docs.text:
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/MohanadAbugharbia/odoo-operator/releases/latest/download/install.yaml
kubectl -n odoo-operator-system rollout status deploy/odoo-operator-controller-manager

This installs the four CRDs (OdooDeployment, OdooBackupStore, OdooBackup, OdooRestore) and runs the manager in odoo-operator-system.

docs.title: 2. Run the sample
docs.text:
The sample installs CloudNativePG

config/samples also installs the CloudNativePG operator, to run a one-instance PostgreSQL cluster: the operator itself into odoo-sample, its CRDs and webhook configurations cluster-wide. Skip the sample on a cluster that already runs CloudNativePG, and point an OdooDeployment at your own PostgreSQL instead.

kubectl create namespace odoo-sample
kubectl kustomize config/samples | kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts -f -

Server-side apply is needed because CloudNativePG's CRDs are too large for the annotation a client-side kubectl apply writes.

docs.title: 3. Wait for it to run
docs.text:
kubectl -n odoo-sample get odoodeployment -w

The instance goes through Pending (until the database is reachable) and Initializing (its odoodeployment-sample-init Job installs the modules) to Running:

NAME                    PHASE     READY   IMAGE                       DATABASE   AGE
odoodeployment-sample   Running   True    mohanadabugharbia/odoo:18   odoo       4m

Lifecycle explains each phase. If it stays in one, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 4. Open Odoo
docs.text:
The operator names everything after the OdooDeployment's metadata.name: here the Service is odoodeployment-sample-http.

kubectl -n odoo-sample port-forward svc/odoodeployment-sample-http 8069:8069

Open http://localhost:8069 and log in as admin with the password admin, the user Odoo creates when it initialises a database. Change it in Odoo's preferences.

The master password, which protects Odoo's database manager, is a different one: the operator generates it into the Secret odoodeployment-sample-admin-password. The database manager is off by default (spec.config.listDb: false).

To reach Odoo without a port-forward, see Expose Odoo.

docs.title: 5. Take a first backup
docs.text:
Backups go to an OdooBackupStore. For a first try, a volume in the cluster will do:

kubectl -n odoo-sample create secret generic backup-key \
  --from-literal=password="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"

# backup.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: backups
  namespace: odoo-sample
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooBackupStore
metadata:
  name: local
  namespace: odoo-sample
spec:
  pvc:
    claimName: backups
  encryptionKeySecret:
    name: backup-key
    key: password

kubectl apply -f backup.yaml
kubectl -n odoo-sample get odoobackupstore local -w     # wait for READY true
kubectl -n odoo-sample patch odoodeployment odoodeployment-sample --type merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"backup":{"stores":["local"]}}}'

Then take a backup:

apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooBackup
metadata:
  name: first
  namespace: odoo-sample
spec:
  odooDeployment: odoodeployment-sample

kubectl -n odoo-sample get odoobackup first -w

(The snapshot ID is shortened here; kubectl shows all 64 characters.)

NAME    INSTANCE                PHASE       SNAPSHOT        STORE   COMPLETED   AGE
first   odoodeployment-sample   Completed   3f9c2a1b5e…     local   20s         1m

A store inside the cluster disappears with it. For real backups, follow Set up production backups.

docs.title: 6. Clean up
docs.text:
kubectl -n odoo-sample delete odoodeployment odoodeployment-sample   # first, while PostgreSQL runs: drops its database
kubectl kustomize config/samples | kubectl delete --ignore-not-found -f -
kubectl delete namespace odoo-sample

The second command removes everything the sample installed, including the CloudNativePG CRDs and webhook configurations it put cluster-wide.

To remove the operator too, see Uninstall.

docs.title: How backups work
docs.text: This page explains what a backup is and where it goes. The guides show how to set up a store, take and schedule backups, restore and run restore drills.

docs.title: Stores and repositories
docs.text: Every store holds restic repositories, one per instance under <path>/<namespace>/<deployment>/, encrypted with the key in encryptionKeySecret (keep a copy of it outside the cluster: without it no backup can be read). The kinds of store and their settings are in Set up a backup store.

docs.title: Taking a backup
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph cluster[Kubernetes cluster]
    op[odoo-operator<br/>one Job per instance at a time]
    odoo[Odoo<br/>keeps running, unless offline]
    job[backup Job]
    pg[(PostgreSQL<br/>the instance's database)]
    fs[(filestore volume)]
  end
  subgraph offsite[Stores]
    store[(first store<br/>restic repository)]
    copies[(other stores<br/>optional)]
  end
  op -- "on schedule or on demand" --> job
  op -. "stops it for an offline backup" .-> odoo
  odoo -- "writes attachments" --> fs
  job -- "1. dump, file list and row counts,<br/>one database snapshot" --> pg
  job -- "2. copy the files" --> fs
  job -- "3. one restic snapshot" --> store
  store -- "4. restic copy" --> copies
  1. The Job dumps the database and, from the same database snapshot, lists the files the database refers to and counts each table's rows.
  2. It copies those files from the filestore. A file deleted since the dump is taken from the previous backup.
  3. It writes dump.sql, manifest.json and filestore/ as one restic snapshot to the first store, then applies retention there.
  4. It copies the snapshot to every other store listed, and applies retention in each.

docs.title: What a backup holds
docs.text: A backup is one restic snapshot holding dump.sql (a plain pg_dump taken with a pg_dump of the server's major), manifest.json (Odoo's own format, plus an operator key) and the filestore/, so it is also what Odoo's database manager restores. Online backups run beside Odoo: the dump, the attachment list and the row counts all come from one database snapshot, so they agree with each other. Files that disappeared from the filestore since (Odoo's attachment cleanup) are taken from the previous backup; attachments in neither are listed in status.missingFileNames and the backup ends CompletedWithWarnings. An online backup waits up to two hours for Odoo's filestore cleanup cron to finish when it is running or due within ten minutes (phase WaitingForFilestoreCleanup). With a ReadWriteOncePod data volume, or consistency: Offline, Odoo is stopped while the backup runs.

docs.title: Phases of an OdooBackup
docs.text:
OdooBackup phase Meaning Pending Waiting for the instance: one backup, restore or cleanup runs at a time, and backups wait for init, upgrades and rollouts. WaitingForFilestoreCleanup Odoo's filestore cleanup runs or is due; tried again every two minutes. Running The Job runs. Completed / CompletedWithWarnings status.snapshotID holds it. PartiallyCompleted The backup is in the first store, but a copy to another store failed; status.copies says why. Failed status.message names the step that failed and the Job to read.

Deleting an OdooBackup does not delete the snapshot, and deleting an instance never deletes its backups.

docs.title: Restoring
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph cluster[Kubernetes cluster]
    restore[OdooRestore<br/>names a backup]
    op[odoo-operator]
    odoo[Odoo<br/>scaled to 0]
    job[restore Job]
    pg[(PostgreSQL<br/>db_restore beside db)]
    fs[(filestore volume<br/>db_restore beside db)]
  end
  store[(store holding<br/>the snapshot)]
  restore --> op
  op -- "1. stop Odoo" --> odoo
  op --> job
  store -- "2. fetch the snapshot" --> job
  job -- "3. load dump.sql" --> pg
  job -- "4. write the files" --> fs
  job -- "5. check, then 6. swap<br/>database and files by renaming" --> pg
  op -- "7. start Odoo" --> odoo

Nothing live changes until the swap:

  1. Odoo is stopped (the maintenance page shows, when enabled).
  2. The Job fetches the snapshot, from a copy in another store when the backup's own store is not ready.
  3. It loads dump.sql into a new database, <db>_restore_<suffix>.
  4. It writes the files into filestore/<db>_restore_<suffix>, beside the live ones.
  5. It checks the result: every table's row count must match the backup and every attachment the backup holds must be there, or the restore stops with the live data untouched. A sample of files is also compared with its checksum; a mismatch is a warning in the OdooRestore's status, since those files were already damaged when the backup was taken.
  6. It swaps by renaming: the live database and files become <db>_prev_<suffix>, kept for keepPrevious (72 hours by default) so the restore can be undone, and the restored ones take their names.
  7. Odoo starts on the image recorded in the backup.

The details, and how to undo a restore, are in Restore and undo.

docs.title: The backup image
docs.text: The Jobs run ghcr.io/mohanadabugharbia/odoo-operator-backup at the operator's own tag (derived from the operator's image; --backup-image overrides it). An operator image pinned by digest only has no tag to derive it from, and gets :latest: set --backup-image for such installs. It carries the PostgreSQL 14–18 clients, restic, rclone and the odoo-backup agent, and runs as the instance's pod security context with no service account token.

docs.title: Databases
docs.text:
How the operator decides whether it owns an instance's database, and when it may drop it.

  • On the first reconcile the operator looks the database up. If it exists it is adopted (status.database.provisionedBy: external). If it is missing and spec.database.createPolicy is IfNotExists (default) the operator creates it — CREATE DATABASE … ENCODING 'unicode' LC_COLLATE 'C' LC_CTYPE 'C' TEMPLATE template0, the same shape Odoo uses — and tags it with the comment odoo-operator:<namespace>/<name> (provisionedBy: operator). It also tries to add the unaccent and pg_trgm extensions, and carries on without them. Restores and drills create databases (restores also rename them) whatever createPolicy says, so for those the database user needs CREATEDB.
  • spec.database.deletionPolicy: Delete adds the finalizer odoo.abugharbia.com/database, unless the database was adopted. On deletion the operator stops the pods and drops the database only if it recorded provisionedBy: operator and the database comment still equals its tag. A CR pointing at a pre-existing database never drops it, whatever the policy says. Dropping uses DROP DATABASE … WITH (FORCE), which needs PostgreSQL 13 or later. If the connection Secret is already gone (for example when the whole namespace is deleted) the database is left in place with a DatabaseNotDropped event.
  • spec.database.name and the nameFromSecret selector are immutable so a rename can never orphan or drop the wrong database. Changing the value inside the Secret that nameFromSecret points at stops the instance instead: phase Failed, Degraded reason DatabaseNameChanged.
  • spec.odooFilestore.deletionPolicy works the same way for the filestore PVC (Retain by default). The PVC is created once: changing spec.odooFilestore.size or storageClassName later does not change it.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
An OdooDeployment moves through status.phase:

Phase Meaning Pending The database connection or the database itself is not settled yet (see the Degraded condition for the reason). Initializing The <name>-init Job installs spec.modules (-i, with --load-language from spec.config.loadLanguages) on spec.image. No Deployment exists yet. Upgrading The new image has been pulled once (see Upgrades); the Deployment is scaled to zero and a <name>-upgrade-<hash> Job runs -i <new modules> / -u <spec.upgrade.modules> on it. Running The Deployment runs status.appliedImage; Ready is True once the requested replicas are available (or spec.replicas is 0). BackingUp An offline backup runs; Odoo is stopped (see How backups work). An online backup leaves the phase alone. Restoring An OdooRestore runs; Odoo is stopped until it finishes. Failed Odoo is stopped and needs attention. Usually a maintenance Job failed: the Degraded condition names the Job and the kubectl logs command to read it. Deleting the Job retries it, and so does its spec.jobs.ttlSecondsAfterFinished (24 hours by default) running out, so read its log before then. Also DatabaseNameChanged (the name resolved from spec.database.nameFromSecret changed) and a restore abandoned in the middle of its swap (RestoreIncomplete).

status.currentInitJob.startedAt records when the running Job was created and status.lastMaintenanceDuration how long the last successful upgrade took.

Conditions: Ready, DatabaseReady, Initialized, BackupSchedule (a backup or drill schedule that cannot be read) and Degraded (True only when something is wrong; its reason names the problem, e.g. DatabaseMissing, InitJobFailed, QuotaExceeded, ImagePullFailed, DatabaseDropFailed).

The <name>-http and <name>-poll Services are created on the first reconcile, before the database and the init Job, so an Ingress pointing at them can be applied together with the CR. They have no endpoints until the Deployment's pods are ready, unless the maintenance page is enabled.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text:
.github/workflows/ci.yml runs on pull requests and on pushes to main. Its first job, Changes, decides which of the others run, so a pull request pays only for the tests its change needs:

Job What it runs Runs on a pull request Runs on main Unit and envtest make test (the envtest suites against a real API server), a check that api/v1/zz_generated.deepcopy.go, config/crd and config/rbac are in sync with the types, and a make build-installer of the release bundle when anything but docs changed when anything but docs changed Lint make lint (golangci-lint) when anything but docs changed when anything but docs changed Backup on PostgreSQL 16–18 hack/backup-it.sh once per major when backup code changed, or with full-ci or backup-ci when anything but docs changed Backup e2e (kind) hack/backup-e2e.sh when backup code changed, or with full-ci or backup-ci when anything but docs changed Images pushes the operator and backup images (amd64 and arm64) tagged sha-<head sha> and pr-<number>, to try a branch on a real cluster with full-ci or images-ci, and only from this repository never
  • Docs means docs/, Markdown files, mkdocs.yml, LICENSE and the Docs workflow. A docs-only change skips every job here.
  • Backup code is the list in the backup filter of the Changes job: the backup agent and its image, the backup and restore types, CRDs and RBAC, the backup controllers and the instance work queue, schedules, go.mod and go.sum, and ci.yml itself. A backup-related change outside that list is still caught by the full run on main; add the path to the filter when that happens.
  • Labels. full-ci runs everything, backup-ci the backup suite and images-ci the images. Adding one of them runs CI again with it, and the newer run replaces the one in progress. Other labels do not start CI.
  • A skipped job counts as passed, so these jobs can be required checks.
  • The Changes job's summary says what ran and why.

.github/workflows/docs.yml builds this site on every pull request, and publishes it from main, from releases and, as a preview, from pull requests with the docs-preview label; see Writing the docs.

docs.title: Test results
docs.text:
The test job runs go test with -json and renders the event stream into a Markdown report with hack/test-summary.py. The report goes to the job summary on every run and, on pull requests, into a single sticky comment that is rewritten in place each time (header go-test-results), so a PR always shows the state of its latest run rather than a trail of comments. The full stream and the coverage profile (plus a rendered coverage.html) are uploaded as artifacts for seven days, and the report links to both.

Two details of the count are worth knowing when reading it:

  • Ginkgo suites are counted in specs, not in Go tests. internal/controller and internal/controller/reconcileloops each expose one Go test to the toolchain (TestControllers) that carries the whole suite, so counting the stream as-is would report 2 tests for ~70 specs. Where a package's output carries Ginkgo's own Ran N of M Specs summary, those numbers are used and the wrapper test is not counted.
  • Only leaf tests count. A table-driven parent with subtests contributes its subtests, not itself.

A package that fails without a failing test — a build error, a panic outside a test, a TestMain failure — is reported as a failure with its output, not silently dropped: go test -json reports a build failure as a separate event shape that names no package.

To get the same report locally:

make test-summary   # writes go-test.json, cover.out and test-summary.md

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• go version v1.25.0+
  • docker version 17.03+.
  • kubectl version v1.28.0+.
  • Access to a Kubernetes v1.28.0+ cluster.

docs.title: Running the tests
docs.text:
make test

This runs the unit suites and the envtest ones (the Kubernetes binaries are downloaded on demand). Coverage is written to cover.out and measured with -coverpkg across every shipped package, so a helper exercised by another package's suite is credited to it; measuring per-package instead understated the project by roughly 25 points.

The internal/database tests that need a real PostgreSQL skip unless one is configured, because they assert the SQL the provisioner emits, the COMMENT that marks operator-owned databases and the refusal to drop a database carrying somebody else's comment. CI starts a postgres:16 service for them. To run them locally against any throwaway server:

TEST_PG_HOST=127.0.0.1 TEST_PG_PORT=5432 \
TEST_PG_USER=postgres TEST_PG_PASSWORD=postgres make test

The backup agent's real-service tests (internal/backup/agent) skip without TEST_BACKUP_PG_HOST (the same variables with a BACKUP_ infix), because they also need restic, rclone and the client tools of the server's major. hack/backup-it.sh runs them inside the backup image against PostgreSQL, an SFTP server and an S3 server it starts in Docker: fidelity of a round trip, the repair from the previous backup, undo, cleanup, and a failure or crash injected at every step of a restore, which must then either leave the live data untouched or finish when run again.

PG_MAJOR=17 hack/backup-it.sh

hack/backup-e2e.sh backs up, restores and undoes a real Odoo in a kind cluster through an S3 store and a PVC store. CI runs both.

make test-e2e additionally needs Docker and kind, and is not part of CI.

docs.title: Deploy a build on a cluster
docs.text:
Build and push your image to the location specified by IMG:

make docker-build docker-push IMG=<some-registry>/odoo-operator:tag

NOTE: This image ought to be published in the personal registry you specified. And it is required to have access to pull the image from the working environment. Make sure you have the proper permission to the registry if the above commands don’t work.

Install the CRDs into the cluster:

make install

Deploy the Manager to the cluster with the image specified by IMG:

make deploy IMG=<some-registry>/odoo-operator:tag

NOTE: If you encounter RBAC errors, you may need to grant yourself cluster-admin privileges or be logged in as admin.

Create instances of your solution You can apply the samples (examples) from the config/sample:

kubectl apply -k config/samples/

NOTE: Ensure that the samples has default values to test it out.

docs.title: Uninstall it
docs.text:
Delete the instances (CRs) from the cluster:

kubectl delete -k config/samples/

Delete the APIs(CRDs) from the cluster:

make uninstall

UnDeploy the controller from the cluster:

make undeploy

The operator is built with Kubebuilder; its book explains the project layout and the make targets.

docs.title: Writing the docs
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs and Material for MkDocs from the docs/ folder, and published to GitHub Pages at https://odoo-operator.abugharbia.com/. A change in behaviour and the change to its page go in the same pull request.

The README stays short: what the operator is, the install command and links here. Usage, operations and internals belong on this site, so a feature pull request edits its page under docs/, not the README.

docs.title: Build and preview locally
docs.text:
make docs-serve    # http://127.0.0.1:8000, reloads on every save
make docs-build    # what CI runs: fails on any warning, such as a broken link

Both create a Python virtual environment under bin/docs-venv from docs/requirements.txt on first use.

docs.title: Generated pages
docs.text:
docs/reference/api.md and docs/reference/metrics.md are generated; do not edit them. After changing a type in api/v1 or a metric in internal/metrics, run:

make docs-reference

and commit the result. CI fails a pull request whose generated pages are stale.

  • The API reference comes from the Go types and their comments, through crd-ref-docs (hack/docs/crd-ref-docs.yaml).
  • The metrics reference comes from the metrics the operator registers (metrics.Reference, written out by hack/docs). A new metric must be added to the registered list in internal/metrics/metrics.go, or to the Collector, to be exported at all, so it cannot be left out of the page.

docs.title: Preview a pull request
docs.text:
Add the docs-preview label to a pull request. The site of that pull request is then published at https://odoo-operator.abugharbia.com/pr-preview/pr-<number>/, a comment on the pull request links to it, and every push updates it. Removing the label or closing the pull request deletes the preview.

Pull requests from forks get no preview: their workflows cannot write to the repository. Every pull request, labelled or not, still builds the site.

docs.title: Set up a backup store
docs.text:
An OdooBackupStore says where backups go. Every store holds encrypted restic repositories, one per instance under <path>/<namespace>/<deployment>/, encrypted with the key in encryptionKeySecret.

Keep the encryption key

Keep a copy of the key in encryptionKeySecret outside the cluster: without it no backup can be read.

apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooBackupStore
metadata:
  name: offsite
  namespace: shop
spec:
  s3:                                 # or sftp, nfs, pvc: exactly one
    endpoint: https://s3.example.com
    bucket: odoo-backups
    path: production
    credentialsSecret: { name: s3-credentials }   # AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  encryptionKeySecret: { name: backup-key, key: password }

docs.title: Kinds of store
docs.text: Kind Fields Secret s3 endpoint (empty for AWS), region, bucket, path, forcePathStyle credentialsSecret: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY sftp host, port (22), user, path sshSecret: the private key under id_ed25519 or ssh-privatekey, and known_hosts (the server's host key; nothing else is trusted) nfs server, path pvc claimName, subPath

docs.title: SFTP keys
docs.text:
The SFTP private key can be any unencrypted Ed25519, ECDSA or RSA key, in OpenSSH or PEM format; a key with a passphrase does not work. The key name only says where the key is, not its type: id_ed25519 is read first, and ssh-privatekey is the key of Secrets of type kubernetes.io/ssh-auth. known_hosts takes the server's host key of any type:

ssh-keyscan -p 22 backup.example.com > known_hosts
kubectl -n shop create secret generic my-odoo-sftp \
  --from-file=id_ed25519=$HOME/.ssh/backup_key --from-file=known_hosts

Check the scanned key against the one the server's provider shows before you trust it.

docs.title: Probes
docs.text:
The operator probes each store with a short Job that writes, reads and deletes a file (.odoo-operator-probe-<random>), on every change to the store or its Secrets and every six hours. kubectl get odoobackupstore shows Ready; a store that fails says why in its Ready condition and in an event, and is probed again every two minutes until it passes. The last failed probe's Job is kept for its log.

To keep a store healthy over time, check and prune it on a schedule.

docs.title: Take and schedule backups
docs.text:
Backups need three objects: a store, the instance pointing at it, and a backup.

apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooBackupStore
metadata:
  name: offsite
  namespace: shop
spec:
  s3:                                 # or sftp, nfs, pvc: exactly one
    endpoint: https://s3.example.com
    bucket: odoo-backups
    path: production
    credentialsSecret: { name: s3-credentials }   # AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  encryptionKeySecret: { name: backup-key, key: password }
---
# in the OdooDeployment
spec:
  backup:
    stores: [offsite]
    consistency: Online               # default; Offline stops Odoo while it runs
---
apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooBackup
metadata:
  name: my-odoo-2026-10-17
  namespace: shop
spec:
  odooDeployment: my-odoo

With a store set up (check that it is Ready: a backup does not wait for that), creating an OdooBackup takes a backup; How backups work explains what it holds and the phases it goes through.

docs.title: Schedules and retention
docs.text:
spec.backup.schedule takes backups on a schedule, and retention decides which old ones are deleted after each backup:

spec:
  backup:
    stores: [offsite, cold]           # the first is written; the others get copies
    schedule: "0 3 * * *"             # cron or @daily; empty (default) = no scheduled backups
    timeZone: Europe/Berlin           # of the schedules and the retention periods (default UTC)
    retention:                        # defaults: daily 7, weekly 4, monthly 12
      daily: 7
      weekly: 4
      monthly: 12
      within: 2d                      # also keep everything from the last 2 days (y, m, d, h)
      manual: 10                      # newest manual backups kept; 0 (default) keeps all
    drill:
      schedule: "0 5 * * 0"           # [restore drill](drills.md)

A scheduled backup is an ordinary OdooBackup named <instance>-<yyyymmdd-hhmm> (the time in timeZone) that waits in the instance's queue like any other. A time missed while the operator was down is taken once when it is back; a time that comes while the previous scheduled backup is still unfinished is skipped with an event. status.backup shows the last and next scheduled times, and the BackupSchedule condition reports a schedule that cannot be read.

Retention runs in the backup Job, after the new backup is verified. The keep rules are restic's (last, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, within, with restic's meaning: within counts back from the newest backup, not from now), but the periods are counted in timeZone, and they apply to scheduled backups; manual backups keep their newest manual. Never deleted: the newest backup, a backup with spec.keep: true (it does not use up a slot of the rules either), a snapshot an unfinished restore needs, and snapshots the operator did not take. The OdooBackups of deleted snapshots are deleted too; a retention that fails leaves the backup Completed with a warning. retention.keepAll: true turns it off. One run deletes at most 24 snapshots, oldest first, so a tightened policy takes a few backups to catch up. Deleting the snapshot frees no space by itself: the store's prune does.

A failed backup is not retried: the next scheduled one, or a new OdooBackup, is the retry. Its Job is kept for spec.jobs.ttlSecondsAfterFinished (24 hours by default) for its log.

docs.title: Copies
docs.text: Each backup is copied (restic copy) to every store after the first in spec.backup.stores, in the same Job, and retention runs in each copy too. A store that is missing or whose Secret is incomplete is skipped; a store that is not ready is still tried. A skipped store or a copy that fails leaves the backup PartiallyCompleted with status.copies saying why; the backup in the first store is still good. A restore (or drill) whose backup's store is not ready restores a copy from a ready store instead, with an event saying so. Stores may use different kinds and different encryption keys.

docs.title: Recover onto a new cluster
docs.text:
When the cluster, or the instance's namespace, is gone, its backups are still in the store. This page restores an instance from them onto a new cluster. You need:

  • the encryption key of the store, kept outside the cluster (see Set up production backups);
  • access to the store (its credentials, SSH key or volume);
  • the instance's old namespace and name;
  • restic on a workstation, to list the backups.

Rehearse it

This procedure follows how the operator finds and restores backups, but the restore onto a never-initialised instance it relies on is not covered by the operator's end-to-end tests yet. Try it on a scratch cluster before you depend on it.

docs.title: Why the name matters
docs.text: An instance's repository in a store is at <path>/<namespace>/<name>/: the store's path, then the OdooDeployment's namespace and metadata.name. The operator finds the backups only if the new instance has the same namespace and name and uses a store with the same location (bucket and path, server and path, export, or volume and subPath) and the same key. The store's own name may differ. Restoring into another namespace or name is not supported.

docs.title: 1. List the backups
docs.text:
The operator keeps no list of snapshots outside the OdooBackups, which went with the old cluster, so read the repository with restic. For an S3 store (endpoint: https://s3.example.com, bucket: odoo-backups, path: production) and the instance shop/my-odoo:

export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=… AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=…
export RESTIC_PASSWORD_FILE=./backup-key.txt          # the saved encryption key
export RESTIC_REPOSITORY=s3:https://s3.example.com/odoo-backups/production/shop/my-odoo
# add -o s3.region=<region> if the store sets one, -o s3.bucket-lookup=path for forcePathStyle

restic snapshots

For AWS itself the repository is s3:s3.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/<path>/<namespace>/<name>; for an SFTP, NFS or volume store point restic at the same folder on that server or volume. Each snapshot is tagged with its instance (deployment=<namespace>/<name>), the OdooBackup that took it (backup=…) and its kind (kind=scheduled, manual or pre-upgrade).

Pick one, and read what it was taken with:

restic dump <snapshot-id> /backup/manifest.json

Note operator.image, operator.upgradeToken and the Odoo version: the new instance should start on the same image.

docs.title: 2. Recreate the namespace, Secrets and store
docs.text:
On the new cluster, with the operator installed:

kubectl create namespace shop
kubectl -n shop create secret generic backup-key --from-file=password=backup-key.txt
kubectl -n shop create secret generic s3-credentials \
  --from-literal=AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=… --from-literal=AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=…

Then the OdooBackupStore, with the same bucket and path as before (the manifest from Set up production backups), and wait until it is Ready.

docs.title: 3. Create the restore first
docs.text:
Create the OdooRestore before the instance. It waits, Pending, until the instance exists, and then runs before the instance's init Job would install anything:

apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooRestore
metadata:
  name: recover
  namespace: shop
spec:
  odooDeployment: my-odoo
  snapshotID: <snapshot-id>      # a unique prefix is enough

docs.title: 4. Create the instance
docs.text:
Create the OdooDeployment as it was, with these points checked:

  • metadata.name: my-odoo and namespace shop, as before;
  • spec.database.createPolicy: IfNotExists (the default): the operator creates an empty database for the restore to replace. With Never and no database the instance stops at DatabaseMissing and the restore never runs;
  • spec.backup.stores lists the recreated store first: a restore by snapshot ID reads only the first store;
  • spec.image and spec.upgrade.token set to the backup's operator.image and operator.upgradeToken, so no upgrade follows the restore;
  • spec.modules limited to modules the backup has; any others are installed after the restore;
  • for now, no spec.backup.schedule, and spec.backup.retention.keepAll: true (see step 6).

The operator creates the filestore volume and an empty database, runs the restore, and starts Odoo on the backup's image:

kubectl -n shop get odoorestore recover -w
kubectl -n shop get odoodeployment my-odoo

The restore ends Completed; any warnings are in status.warnings. The empty database it replaced is kept as <db>_prev_<suffix> for keepPrevious, then deleted.

docs.title: 5. Check Odoo
docs.text: Log in, check recent records and attachments, and only then point users and the Ingress at the new instance.

docs.title: 6. Turn backups back on
docs.text: Set the schedule again. Before you remove keepAll, know that retention on the new instance applies to the old snapshots too: they carry the same host and tags, so the daily, weekly and monthly rules thin them like new ones. Old snapshots cannot be pinned one by one, so keep keepAll: true until you no longer need them.

docs.title: Restoring from a copy
docs.text: If the first store is lost too, restore from a copy: list the copy's store first in spec.backup.stores and use the snapshot ID in that store (restic snapshots against the copy's repository; a copy has its own ID).

docs.title: Restore drills
docs.text: A drill proves the newest backup can be restored, without touching the instance: on spec.backup.drill.schedule it waits in the instance's queue, then one Job restores the newest finished backup into a scratch database <db>_drill_<suffix> and a scratch filestore on an emptyDir (never the data volume), runs the same checks as a restore, has the backup's own Odoo image read it (odoo shell -d <db>_drill_<suffix>, run through sh: Odoo loads its registry, reads records of core models and reads attachments from the scratch filestore), and drops the scratch database. Odoo keeps serving throughout. The outcome is in status.backup.lastDrill (lastSuccessfulDrillTime keeps the last pass); a failed drill keeps its Job for spec.jobs.ttlSecondsAfterFinished (kubectl logs job/<name> --all-containers). The scratch filestore needs node disk the size of the filestore; drill.scratchSizeLimit caps it.

docs.title: Expose Odoo
docs.text:
Every instance gets two Services, named after its metadata.name:

Service Port Serves <name>-http 8069 Odoo's web interface and RPC <name>-poll 8072 Odoo's live-update channel (/websocket; /longpolling before Odoo 16), when Odoo runs with workers

Both exist from the first reconcile, before the database and the init Job, so an Ingress can be applied together with the OdooDeployment. They have no endpoints until Odoo's pods are ready, unless the maintenance page is on: then <name>-http points at it while Odoo is installed, upgraded or started. <name>-poll always points at Odoo.

docs.title: Route the live-update channel
docs.text:
With spec.config.workers above 0 (the default is 2), Odoo serves live updates (chat, notifications, the POS) from a separate process on port 8072. Send /websocket there and everything else to port 8069. With ingress-nginx (the annotations are its own; other controllers have equivalents):

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: shop
  namespace: shop
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size: 100m     # uploads and imports
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "720"  # long requests and the websocket
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts: [odoo.example.com]
      secretName: odoo-example-com-tls
  rules:
    - host: odoo.example.com
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /websocket
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service: {name: my-odoo-poll, port: {number: 8072}}
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service: {name: my-odoo-http, port: {number: 8069}}

With workers: 0 Odoo runs threaded and serves everything, live updates included, on port 8069: the /websocket rule is then not needed.

docs.title: Proxy mode
docs.text: spec.config.proxyMode is true by default: Odoo then trusts the X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto headers for the client address, host and scheme (Odoo applies them only when the proxy also sends X-Forwarded-Host; ingress-nginx does). Behind an Ingress controller that sets them, keep it on; reaching Odoo directly, without a proxy that sets them, turn it off.

docs.title: Grafana dashboard
docs.text:
The repository ships a Grafana dashboard for the operator's metrics: config/grafana/odoo-operator-dashboard.json.

The top of the dashboard, with sample data: two instances, one of them Degraded after an image pull failure.

docs.title: What it shows
docs.text:
Row Panels Instances how many OdooDeployments are in each phase, whether the operator is up, and a table of every instance with its phase, image and applied image Health Degraded instances with their reason, pending image changes, and desired against available replicas Phases the phase of every instance over time Init and upgrade Jobs the Jobs running now and for how long, finished Jobs by result, Job duration (median and 95th percentile), image pull failures, database operations Backups time since each instance's last successful backup, failed backups and copies, missing attachments, scheduled instances, backup sizes, finished backups by kind and result, backup duration Restores and drills time since each instance's last passing drill, failed drills and restores, restores and undos by result Backup stores whether each store is ready, time since its last check and prune, failed checks and prunes, and what it holds Odoo pods CPU, memory against its limit, restarts, and how full each filestore volume is Operator reconciles, reconcile errors and time, the work queue, the manager's memory, API client errors, and the running version

The thresholds of "time since" panels (backups: a day and two, drills and store tasks: eight and fifteen days) suit a daily backup and a weekly drill; change them to your schedules, as with the example alerts.

The selectors at the top pick the Prometheus data source and the operator's scrape job, and narrow the panels to some namespaces, instances and stores.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Prometheus (or a compatible store such as Mimir or Thanos) scraping the manager's /metrics; Monitoring and alerts shows how. The Operator job selector lists the jobs that export odoo_operator_build_info; with a ServiceMonitor on the install bundle's metrics Service it is odoo-operator-controller-manager-metrics-service.
  • The scrape must keep the series' own namespace label (honorLabels: true on a ServiceMonitor, honor_labels: true in a scrape config): the per-instance series carry the namespace of their OdooDeployment, which Prometheus would otherwise rename to exported_namespace, leaving the namespace selector with only the operator's namespace.
  • kube-state-metrics for the replica counts in the Instances table and the Health row.
  • For the Odoo pods row: the kubelet's cAdvisor and volume metrics (container_cpu_usage_seconds_total, container_memory_working_set_bytes, kubelet_volume_stats_*) and kube-state-metrics (kube_pod_container_resource_limits, kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total). Without them that row stays empty and the rest works.

docs.title: Import it
docs.text:
In Grafana, Dashboards → New → Import, paste the JSON (or the raw URL of the file), and pick your Prometheus data source.

With the Grafana Helm chart's dashboard sidecar, a ConfigMap with the grafana_dashboard label loads it instead:

# kustomization.yaml
configMapGenerator:
  - name: dashboard-odoo-operator
    files:
      - odoo-operator.json=odoo-operator-dashboard.json
generatorOptions:
  disableNameSuffixHash: true
  labels:
    grafana_dashboard: "1"

The dashboard's uid is odoo-operator, so links to it stay valid across imports.

docs.title: Maintenance page
docs.text:
An upgrade in progress, with the default branding (title "Odoo", colour #714b67).

With spec.maintenancePage.enabled: true, a browser opening the instance while Odoo cannot answer gets a status page instead of a blank screen:

spec:
  maintenancePage:
    enabled: true
    title: My Shop            # default "Odoo"
    titleTranslations:
      ar: متجري
    accentColor: "#f2800d"    # default "#714b67"
    logo: data:image/svg+xml;base64,…   # optional, data URIs only
  • Whenever Odoo's Deployment has no available replica (first setup, an upgrade, a restart) and spec.replicas is not 0, the operator runs a <name>-maintenance Deployment (one pod, 10m CPU / 32Mi) and points the <name>-http Service's selector at it. Once Odoo has an available replica the selector moves back and the page scales to zero. The <name>-poll Service always stays on Odoo.
  • The pod runs the operator's own image (odoo-operator maintenance-page), so there is nothing extra to build or pin. The operator reads its image from its own pod, retrying on each reconcile until it succeeds (a failure shows as a MaintenancePageImageUnknown warning event on the OdooDeployment); --maintenance-page-image overrides it.
  • The page needs no access to the API server: after every reconcile the operator writes what the page shows into the <name>-maintenance ConfigMap, which the pod mounts (no ServiceAccount token). On each change it also stamps the status hash on the page pods (odoo.abugharbia.com/maintenance-status), which makes the kubelet refresh the mount at once instead of on its next periodic sync, up to a minute later.
  • It answers like a server that is down, so Odoo's own clients keep their offline behaviour: a page navigation (Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate) gets the page with status 503, and every other request (RPC, assets, /web/health, service worker fetches) gets an empty 503. Nothing is cacheable.
  • The page shows the phase as steps (preparing the database, installing, updating, starting), the elapsed time and, for upgrades, an estimate from status.lastMaintenanceDuration. It polls /__maintenance/status.json and /web/health every 3 seconds, and reopens the URL that was asked for as soon as Odoo answers. A failed Job shows only "Please contact your administrator"; the reason stays in the CR's conditions and events.
  • English or Arabic (right to left) is picked from the browser's Accept-Language; it follows the device's light or dark mode, and loads no external fonts or scripts.

docs.title: Monitoring and alerts
docs.text: The manager serves /metrics on :8443 over HTTPS, with Kubernetes authentication and authorization, through the odoo-operator-controller-manager-metrics-service Service. That port comes from the install bundle (--metrics-bind-address=:8443); the binary alone serves no metrics. --metrics-bind-address=:8080 --metrics-secure=false serves plain HTTP instead. Besides the controller-runtime defaults (controller_runtime_reconcile_*, workqueue_*, rest_client_*, Go and process metrics) it exports the series in the metrics reference.

docs.title: Scrape it
docs.text:
The install bundle does not include a ServiceMonitor. With the Prometheus Operator, this one scrapes the HTTPS endpoint:

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: odoo-operator
  namespace: odoo-operator-system
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      control-plane: controller-manager
  endpoints:
    - port: https
      path: /metrics
      scheme: https
      bearerTokenFile: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token
      tlsConfig:
        insecureSkipVerify: true   # the manager's certificate is self-signed
      honorLabels: true
  • honorLabels: true is required. The per-instance series carry the namespace of their OdooDeployment in namespace; without it Prometheus renames that label to exported_namespace, and the alerts and the dashboard lose it.
  • Prometheus needs read access to /metrics. Bind its service account to the odoo-operator-metrics-reader ClusterRole, which the bundle installs.
  • config/prometheus/ holds the same ServiceMonitor and the example alerts as a kustomize base. It is not part of the install bundle.

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text: config/prometheus/backup-alerts.yaml holds example alerts on these metrics (stale or failed backups, failed copies, restores and drills, stores that are not ready or fail their check or prune). Adjust the staleness thresholds to your schedules.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: A ready-made Grafana dashboard for these metrics is described in Grafana dashboard.

docs.title: Set up production backups
docs.text: This walkthrough sets up what a production instance should have: encrypted backups offsite on a schedule, a copy in a second place, a weekly restore drill, regular store checks, and alerts. It uses an instance my-odoo in the namespace shop, an S3 bucket as the first store and an SFTP server as the second; Set up a backup store has the other kinds.

docs.title: 1. Create the encryption key, and keep a copy
docs.text:
Every store encrypts its repositories with a key from a Secret. Generate a long random one:

openssl rand -base64 32 > backup-key.txt
kubectl -n shop create secret generic backup-key --from-file=password=backup-key.txt

Without the key, no backup can be read

Store backup-key.txt outside the cluster now, in a password manager or a vault. If the cluster is lost, it is the only way to read the backups: see Recover onto a new cluster. Then delete the local file.

Both stores here use the same key; each store may also have its own.

docs.title: 2. Create the stores
docs.text:
The S3 credentials, under the two keys the operator reads:

kubectl -n shop create secret generic s3-credentials \
  --from-literal=AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=… \
  --from-literal=AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=…

The SFTP key and the server's host key (SFTP keys has the details):

ssh-keyscan backup.example.com > known_hosts     # check it against the server's key
kubectl -n shop create secret generic sftp-key \
  --from-file=id_ed25519=$HOME/.ssh/backup_key --from-file=known_hosts

# stores.yaml
apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooBackupStore
metadata:
  name: offsite
  namespace: shop
spec:
  s3:
    endpoint: https://s3.example.com      # leave out for AWS
    region: eu-central-1
    bucket: odoo-backups
    path: production
    credentialsSecret: {name: s3-credentials}
  encryptionKeySecret: {name: backup-key, key: password}
  check:
    schedule: "0 4 * * 0"                 # Sundays: verify the repositories
    readDataParts: 7                      # read a seventh of the data each time
  prune:
    schedule: "0 2 * * 6"                 # Saturdays: free the space of old backups
  timeZone: Europe/Berlin
---
apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooBackupStore
metadata:
  name: cold
  namespace: shop
spec:
  sftp:
    host: backup.example.com
    user: odoo
    path: backups
    sshSecret: {name: sftp-key}
  encryptionKeySecret: {name: backup-key, key: password}
  prune:
    schedule: "0 3 * * 6"
  timeZone: Europe/Berlin

kubectl apply -f stores.yaml
kubectl -n shop get odoobackupstore

Wait until both show READY true. A store that is not ready says why in its REASON column and in kubectl -n shop describe odoobackupstore <store>.

docs.title: 3. Schedule backups on the instance
docs.text:
# in the OdooDeployment my-odoo
spec:
  backup:
    stores: [offsite, cold]     # backups go to offsite, and are copied to cold
    schedule: "0 3 * * *"       # every night at 03:00
    timeZone: Europe/Berlin
    retention:                  # keep 7 daily, 4 weekly and 12 monthly backups
      daily: 7
      weekly: 4
      monthly: 12
      manual: 10                # and the 10 newest manual ones
    drill:
      schedule: "0 5 * * 0"     # Sundays: prove the newest backup restores

Take and schedule backups explains the retention rules, what is never deleted, and copies; Restore drills what a drill checks.

docs.title: 4. Take a first backup now, and check it
docs.text:
Don't wait for the schedule:

apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooBackup
metadata:
  name: my-odoo-first
  namespace: shop
spec:
  odooDeployment: my-odoo
  keep: true                    # never removed by retention

kubectl -n shop get odoobackup my-odoo-first -w
kubectl -n shop get odoobackup my-odoo-first -o jsonpath='{.status.copies}'

It should end Completed, with a copy in cold in status.copies. PartiallyCompleted means the backup is in offsite but the copy failed; CompletedWithWarnings lists what is missing in status.message and status.missingFileNames. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 5. Watch it
docs.text: Scrape the operator's metrics and install the example alerts, as Monitoring and alerts describes. They fire when a backup is stale or failed, a copy failed, a drill failed or is overdue, or a store is not ready or fails its check or prune. The Grafana dashboard shows the same on one screen.

docs.title: 6. Try a restore
docs.text: A backup you have never restored is a hope. The drill restores the newest backup into scratch space every week without touching the instance. Once, in a maintenance window, also do a real restore and its undo, following Restore and undo, so the steps are known before they are needed.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• The encryption key is stored outside the cluster.
  • Both stores are Ready.
  • A first backup is Completed, with its copy.
  • Scheduled backups appear (kubectl -n shop get odoobackup).
  • status.backup.lastDrill.succeeded is true after the first drill.
  • The stores' status.lastCheck and status.lastPrune pass.
  • The alerts are loaded, and reach someone.

docs.title: Restore and undo
docs.text:
A restore replaces the instance's database and filestore in place:

apiVersion: odoo.abugharbia.com/v1
kind: OdooRestore
metadata:
  name: back-to-friday
  namespace: shop
spec:
  odooDeployment: my-odoo
  backup: my-odoo-2026-10-17        # or snapshotID: <id> in the instance's store
  keepPrevious: 72h                 # default spec.backup.restore.keepPrevious (72h)

Odoo is stopped; the backup is loaded into <db>_restore_<suffix> and filestore/<db>_restore_<suffix> beside the live data and checked: every table's row count must match the backup and every attachment the backup holds must be there. A sample of files is also compared with its checksum; a mismatch only adds a warning to status.warnings, as those files were damaged before the backup. Only then are the names swapped: the live data becomes <db>_prev_<suffix> and the restored data takes its place, and Odoo starts on the image recorded in the backup. A restore that fails before the swap leaves the live data untouched (Failed); one that fails during the swap is retried until it finishes, with Odoo stopped and the instance Degraded (RestoreIncomplete). A restore takes precedence over everything else and replaces a failed init or upgrade Job, which makes it the way back from a failed upgrade. Modules in spec.modules that the backup lacks are installed again afterwards.

The instance then counts as running the backup's image and upgrade token. If spec.image differs from the backup's image, the usual upgrade follows when spec.upgrade.onImageChange is true; if spec.upgrade.token differs from the backup's, an upgrade follows either way. Set both to the backup's values first to stay on it.

A restore by backup falls back to a copy in another store when the backup's store is not ready. A restore by snapshotID reads only the first store in spec.backup.stores.

docs.title: What a restore needs
docs.text:
• Room: the restored files sit beside the live ones on the data volume until the swap, so it needs free space for a second filestore, and the database server holds two to three copies of the database for a while (live, restored, and the previous one kept for undo).
  • Database privileges: a restore always creates and renames databases, whatever spec.database.createPolicy says, so the database user needs CREATEDB.
  • Downtime: Odoo is stopped from the start of the restore to the end of the swap. With a ReadWriteOncePod data volume it is stopped again, briefly, when the kept data is deleted after keepPrevious.

docs.title: What happens if something goes wrong
docs.text:
The live data is never edited in place, so a restore can fail without damaging it, and a Job that dies halfway finishes when it is retried:

flowchart TD
  start([OdooRestore: Odoo is stopped]) --> load["Load the backup beside the live data:<br/>database db_restore_suffix, its filestore"]
  load --> check[Check row counts, attachments<br/>and a sample of checksums]
  load -->|error| failed([Failed: live data untouched])
  check -->|row counts differ or<br/>attachments missing| failed
  check --> swap["Swap: live becomes db_prev_suffix,<br/>restored becomes db"]
  swap -->|Job dies| retry["Retried Job reads the journal<br/>and finishes the swap<br/>(Degraded: RestoreIncomplete meanwhile)"]
  retry --> swap
  swap --> run[Odoo starts on the backup's image]
  run --> kept["Previous data kept until<br/>status.previous.keptUntil"]
  kept -->|OdooRestore with undo| undo[Swap the previous data back]
  kept -->|keptUntil passes| gone([Previous data deleted])

docs.title: Undo a restore
docs.text:
The replaced data is kept until status.previous.keptUntil, then deleted. Until then the restore can be undone:

spec:
  odooDeployment: my-odoo
  undo: back-to-friday

Only the latest restore can be undone. Deleting an OdooRestore deletes the data it kept.

Deleting the instance keeps the previous data

Deleting an OdooDeployment does not delete the <db>_prev_<suffix> databases and folders its restores kept; drop them by hand.

docs.title: Check and prune a store
docs.text:
On their own schedules a store's repositories are checked (restic check) and pruned (restic prune, which frees the space of deleted backups):

spec:                                 # OdooBackupStore
  check:
    schedule: "0 4 * * 0"
    readDataParts: 7                  # each check reads 1/7 of the data, all of it over 7 checks;
                                      # 1 = everything every time, 0 = structure only
  prune:
    schedule: "0 2 * * 6"
  timeZone: Europe/Berlin

Checks and prunes only run while the store is Ready. One Job runs at a time per store, prune first when both are due, over the repositories of every instance in the namespace that lists the store. The outcome is in status.lastCheck and status.lastPrune (with the part read, the repositories and what they hold); a failed task keeps its Job for its log and warns. A backup that starts while a prune holds a repository's lock waits up to half an hour for it.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
Remove your instances first, while the operator still runs: it is the operator that applies their deletion policies.

kubectl delete odoodeployments --all --all-namespaces

What stays behind depends on each instance's policies:

  • The database is dropped only with spec.database.deletionPolicy: Delete, and only when the operator created it (see Databases).
  • The filestore volume is kept unless spec.odooFilestore.deletionPolicy is Delete.
  • Backups are never deleted: deleting an instance or an OdooBackup leaves the snapshots in their stores. The instance's repositories are no longer checked or pruned either, since store tasks only cover instances that list the store.
  • The databases and folders that restores kept for undo (<db>_prev_<suffix>) stay; drop them by hand.
  • Deleting an instance waits for all its pods to stop, including a running backup Job.

Then remove the operator, its CRDs and RBAC:

kubectl delete -f https://github.com/MohanadAbugharbia/odoo-operator/releases/latest/download/install.yaml

Deleting the CRDs deletes every remaining OdooDeployment, OdooBackup, OdooRestore and OdooBackupStore with them. Use the release you installed if it is not the latest.

docs.title: Upgrade Odoo
docs.text:
An upgrade runs Odoo's -u on the database in a Job, with the Deployment scaled to zero, whenever the image changes or you ask for it.

flowchart TD
  trigger["spec.image changes (onImageChange: true)<br/>or spec.upgrade.token changes"]
  check["image check Job<br/>pulls the new image, runs odoo --version<br/>(skipped when the image is unchanged)"]
  old["old image keeps serving<br/>Degraded: ImagePullFailed or ImageCheckFailed"]
  modules{"spec.upgrade.modules<br/>empty?"}
  roll["roll the Deployment<br/>to the new image, no Job"]
  stop["scale Odoo to 0<br/>phase Upgrading"]
  job["upgrade Job<br/>-u spec.upgrade.modules,<br/>-i new spec.modules"]
  running["Odoo starts on the new image<br/>phase Running"]
  failed["phase Failed, Odoo stays stopped<br/>delete the Job to retry (it is also retried<br/>when its TTL removes it), or restore a backup"]

  trigger --> check
  check -- "cannot pull or run" --> old
  old -- "a later spec.image replaces the check" --> check
  check -- "succeeds" --> modules
  modules -- yes --> roll --> running
  modules -- no --> stop --> job
  job -- succeeds --> running
  job -- fails --> failed
  • spec.upgrade.onImageChange: true (default): every spec.image change runs an upgrade Job with -u <spec.upgrade.modules> before the Deployment rolls to the new image. New entries in spec.modules are installed in the same Job.
  • Empty spec.upgrade.modules rolls the new image without a Job.
  • A new image is pulled before anything stops. When spec.image changes on a running instance, a short <name>-image-<hash> Job runs <odooCommand> --version on it first, without the filestore or the config. Only once it succeeds is the Deployment scaled down (or rolled). Until then the old image keeps serving; if the image cannot be pulled Degraded is ImagePullFailed (or ImageCheckFailed when it pulled but did not run), and a later spec.image replaces the check. This is what keeps an instance up when its image tag is published before the image is pushed, or never is.
  • An init or upgrade Job whose pod cannot pull its image is reported as ImagePullFailed. If spec.image changes meanwhile, the Job is replaced by one for the new image: its container never started, so nothing touched the database.
  • For production set onImageChange: false and bump spec.upgrade.token to run the upgrade on demand. A spec.image change then does nothing until the token changes, with one exception: a new entry in spec.modules is installed by a Job on spec.image, and the instance moves to that image without -u.
  • A failed Job is retried when it is deleted, by you or by its ttlSecondsAfterFinished (24 hours by default): the upgrade then runs again on its own. Read the Job's log before that, or restore a backup.
  • spec.jobs bounds the Jobs (activeDeadlineSeconds, ttlSecondsAfterFinished, backoffLimit).

A failed upgrade can be rolled back by restoring a backup: a restore replaces a failed init or upgrade Job.

docs.title: Where to look first
docs.text:
kubectl -n <ns> get odoodeployment <name>             # phase, Ready
kubectl -n <ns> describe odoodeployment <name>        # conditions and events
kubectl -n <ns> get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=<name>
kubectl -n <ns> get odoobackup,odoorestore,odoobackupstore

When something is wrong, the instance's Degraded condition is True and its reason names the problem; a failed Job's event and message include the kubectl logs command to read it.

docs.title: Stuck in Pending
docs.text:
Read the Degraded reason:

Reason Meaning Fix Retried InvalidSpec A key in spec.config.extraOptions is not a valid option name (^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$). Fix the key. On the spec change DatabaseConnectionFailed ("could not resolve…") A Secret or key named by spec.database.*FromSecret (or passwordFromSecret) does not exist. Create the Secret or key. Every 30 s, and when the Secret changes DatabaseConnectionFailed PostgreSQL is unreachable or refuses the credentials. Fix the host, credentials or network. Every 30 s DatabaseProvisioning The operator is about to create the database. — Every 10 s DatabaseCreateFailed CREATE DATABASE failed. Give the role CREATEDB, or create the database yourself. Every 30 s DatabaseMissing The database does not exist and createPolicy is Never. Create it, or set createPolicy: IfNotExists. Every minute QuotaExceeded A ResourceQuota rejected the init Job's pod. Raise the quota or lower spec.resources. Every 15 s

The Services and the maintenance page already exist, except when the reason is InvalidSpec or the "could not resolve…" form of DatabaseConnectionFailed.

docs.title: Stuck in Initializing or Upgrading
docs.text:
The <name>-init or <name>-upgrade-<hash> Job is running; Ready says "waiting for job …". Look at it:

kubectl -n <ns> get pods -l job-name=<job>
kubectl -n <ns> logs job/<job>

ImagePullFailed means the Job's pod cannot pull spec.image: push the image, fix the pull secret, or change spec.image (the Job is then replaced). A Job that runs past spec.jobs.activeDeadlineSeconds (one hour by default) fails.

docs.title: Failed
docs.text: Cause Reason What to do The init or upgrade Job failed InitJobFailed, UpgradeJobFailed, QuotaExceeded Read kubectl -n <ns> logs job/<job>, fix the cause, then delete the Job to retry: changing the spec alone does not. Left alone, the Job is deleted by its TTL (spec.jobs.ttlSecondsAfterFinished, a day by default) and then runs again by itself. A failed upgrade leaves Odoo stopped; restoring a backup replaces the failed Job (Restore and undo). The database name changed DatabaseNameChanged spec.database.name (or the Secret value behind nameFromSecret) now resolves to another name than the instance uses. Put the old value back; the operator never switches databases. A restore was deleted halfway through its swap RestoreIncomplete Odoo stays stopped. Check the <db>_restore_* / <db>_prev_* databases and filestore folders named in the restore Job's log, put the data right, then clear status.currentOperation on the OdooDeployment.

docs.title: A new image is not rolled out
docs.text: What you see Meaning Degraded ImagePullFailed, the old image still serving The <name>-image-<hash> check could not pull the new spec.image. Push it or fix the pull secret; retried every 15 s. Degraded ImageCheckFailed The image pulled but <odooCommand> --version failed. Read kubectl logs job/<name>-image-<hash>, fix the image, then delete that Job to check again. Nothing happens spec.upgrade.onImageChange is false: a new image is applied only when spec.upgrade.token changes. See Upgrade Odoo.

docs.title: The maintenance page does not appear
docs.text: It needs spec.maintenancePage.enabled: true, spec.replicas above 0, and an Odoo Deployment with no available replica. A MaintenancePageImageUnknown warning event means the operator could not read its own image from its pod; set --maintenance-page-image (Operator flags).

docs.title: Other Degraded reasons
docs.text: PvcCreationFailed, OdooConfigSecretCreationFailed, OdooAdminSecretCreationFailed, FailedCreateHttpService, FailedCreatePollService, MaintenancePageFailed, DeploymentFailed, JobCreationFailed and ReconcileFailed mean a Kubernetes API call failed; the message carries the API error (often RBAC, a quota or an invalid field). They are retried with backoff. BackupImageUnknown means the operator could not derive the backup image: set --backup-image. DrillRunning as a Degraded reason means the drill Job's pod cannot start (an image pull or a quota); Deleting and DatabaseDropFailed appear while the instance is deleted (see below).

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
What you see Meaning What to do Pending, "queued on …" Waiting its turn: one backup, restore, drill or cleanup runs at a time per instance, and backups wait for the init Job, upgrades, a failed init or upgrade Job, and older backups. Clear what is ahead; see the instance's status.currentOperation. Pending, "waiting for OdooDeployment … which does not exist" spec.odooDeployment names no instance in the namespace. Fix the name. WaitingForFilestoreCleanup Odoo's attachment cleanup (base.autovacuum_job) runs or is due. Nothing: retried every 2 minutes, and run anyway after 2 hours. Failed, "has no spec.backup.stores" or a store or Secret error Checked before the Job starts. Fix the instance or store, then create a new OdooBackup. Failed, "job … failed at step …" The Job failed at that step (connect, dump, filestore, upload, verify…). kubectl -n <ns> logs job/<job>; the Job is kept until its TTL. Create a new OdooBackup to retry; a scheduled backup tries again at its next time. CompletedWithWarnings The backup is good, but some attachments were in neither the filestore nor the previous backup. status.missingFileNames lists them. PartiallyCompleted The backup is in the first store, but a copy failed. status.copies says why; fix the copy's store.

A failed backup is final: the operator does not retry it. The BackupFailed, BackupCopyFailed and RetentionFailed events, and the example alerts, report failures.

docs.title: Restores
docs.text: What you see Meaning What to do Failed with a RestoreRefused event The restore was refused before it started: the backup does not exist, is of another instance, has not completed, the store is missing, the undo target is gone or not the latest. Read status.message; create a corrected OdooRestore. Failed, "the live data was not changed" The Job failed before the swap. kubectl -n <ns> logs job/<job>; nothing to undo. Restoring for long, instance Degraded RestoreIncomplete The Job failed after the swap may have started; it is retried, from 30 seconds up to every 15 minutes, until it finishes. Odoo stays stopped meanwhile. Fix the cause (store, database); it carries on by itself. Stopping Waiting for Odoo's pods to stop. —

docs.title: Backup stores
docs.text:
Reason in kubectl get odoobackupstore Meaning Retried InvalidSpec The store's spec cannot be used. On the spec change SecretMissing A Secret or a key in it is missing. Every minute, and when the Secret appears Probing The probe Job runs; "cannot start" means it cannot pull the backup image. Every 10 s; the probe fails after 5 minutes StoreUnreachable The probe could not write, read or delete a file. The message has the kubectl logs command for the probe Job. Every 2 minutes StoreReachable Ready. Probed again every 6 hours

A Schedules condition that is False (InvalidSchedule) means spec.check.schedule or spec.prune.schedule does not parse. Checks and prunes run only while the store is ready; a failed one keeps its Job (named in status.lastCheck.job or status.lastPrune.job) for a day, its TTL, or until the next run if that comes sooner.

docs.title: Restore drills
docs.text:
status.backup.lastDrill has the outcome. A failed drill keeps its Job, named in status.backup.lastDrill.job; its log spans several containers:

kubectl -n <ns> logs job/<job> --all-containers

docs.title: Deleting an instance hangs
docs.text:
With spec.database.deletionPolicy: Delete, deletion waits for the instance's pods to stop, including running backup, restore, drill and cleanup Jobs (up to their deadline), and then drops the database. A DatabaseDropFailed event means the drop keeps failing (retried every 30 seconds): fix the database access, or set deletionPolicy: Retain to skip the drop. A database the operator did not create is never dropped. A DatabaseDropRefused event means the database no longer carries the operator's owner tag; DatabaseNotDropped that the connection could not be resolved, so the operator could not drop it.

An OdooRestore stays until its cleanup has deleted the data it kept, or until its instance is gone.

docs.title: Reading a Job's result
docs.text:
Backup, restore, probe and store Jobs write their result as JSON into the termination message of their backup container, besides the log:

kubectl -n <ns> get pods -l job-name=<job> \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="backup")].state.terminated.message}'

docs.title: Upgrading the operator
docs.text: Read the notes of every version between the one you run and the one you install.

• list_db is now False by default and dbfilter = ^<db_name>$ is rendered, so an instance only sees its own database. Set spec.config.listDb: true (and optionally dbFilter) to keep the database manager.
  • spec.database.ssl is rendered as db_sslmode = require / disable (previously it was ignored and Odoo used prefer).
  • spec.database.name and spec.database.nameFromSecret are immutable.
  • spec.replicas, spec.config.workers, maxCronThreads, withoutDemo and proxyMode are pointer fields: 0 and false are now honoured.
  • Existing CRs roll their pods once (new labels, config-hash annotation, probes) and adopt the running image as status.appliedImage without a Job. Their database is adopted as external and is never dropped.
  • The OperatorDegraded/OperatorSucceeded conditions are replaced by Ready, DatabaseReady, Initialized and Degraded.
  • The admin and config Secrets and both Services are now owned by the CR and are garbage collected with it.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The operator renders odoo.conf from spec.config and spec.database; every field is in the API reference.

docs.title: Container command
docs.text: spec.odooCommand (default ["odoo"]) plus -c /opt/odoo/odoo.conf becomes the container command, which replaces the image ENTRYPOINT. Images whose entrypoint script injects database flags (e.g. the official image's entrypoint.sh) are bypassed on purpose: the operator's rendered odoo.conf is the only configuration source. The image's own addons_path and server_wide_modules must therefore be re-expressed in spec.config.extraAddonsPaths and spec.config.serverWideModules.

docs.title: When Odoo restarts
docs.text: The Deployment uses the Recreate strategy, and its pods carry a hash of the rendered odoo.conf. Any change that changes the file restarts Odoo with a short downtime: a spec.config change, but also a new database password in the connection Secret. The operator owns the Deployment's pod template, so changes made to it by hand are reverted.

docs.title: Master password
docs.text: Odoo's master password (admin_passwd, which guards the database manager) is read from the Secret <name>-admin-password, key password, or from the Secret named in spec.config.adminPasswordSecretName. When the key is empty the operator generates a password once; it never rotates it. A Secret you name yourself is not deleted with the instance.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
The words these pages use, and what each one means here.

Instance One Odoo installation: an OdooDeployment and everything it owns (its database, filestore volume, Deployment, Services and Jobs). Its metadata.name, written <name> in these pages, names all of them: <name>-http, <name>-init, <name>-admin-password (unless spec.config.adminPasswordSecretName names another Secret). spec.name is required but not used. Store An OdooBackupStore: a place backups go (an S3 bucket, an SFTP server, an NFS export or a volume) and the key they are encrypted with. See Set up a backup store. Repository The restic repository of one instance inside a store, at <path>/<namespace>/<name>/. A store holds one repository per instance that uses it. Backup An OdooBackup, and the restic snapshot it took: dump.sql, manifest.json and the filestore at one moment. status.snapshotID links the two. Deleting an OdooBackup leaves its snapshot in the store; retention forgets snapshots and deletes their OdooBackups. Scheduled backup / manual backup A scheduled backup is one the operator creates from spec.backup.schedule, named <name>-<yyyymmdd-hhmm>; a manual backup is one you create. Retention thins scheduled backups by its rules; manual backups are kept unless you set retention.manual. Copy The same snapshot copied (restic copy) to every store after the first in spec.backup.stores. Prune Freeing the space of forgotten snapshots in a store (restic prune). Retention only forgets; a store's prune reclaims the space. Check Verifying a store's repositories (restic check), reading a part of the data each time. Probe The short Job that writes, reads and deletes a file in a store to decide whether it is Ready. Restore An OdooRestore: replacing an instance's database and filestore with a backup's, in place. See Restore and undo. Suffix The UTC time a restore started, as 20261018T143000. It names the data a restore creates beside the live data: <db>_restore_<suffix> while it loads, <db>_prev_<suffix> for the replaced data afterwards. A drill's scratch database is <db>_drill_<suffix>. The OdooRestore records it in status.suffix. Previous data / keptUntil The database and filestore a restore replaced, kept as <db>_prev_<suffix> until status.previous.keptUntil (keepPrevious, 72 hours by default) so the restore can be undone. Undo An OdooRestore with spec.undo, which swaps the previous data back. Drill A scheduled test restore of the newest backup into scratch space, beside the instance, which keeps serving. It proves the backup can be restored. See Restore drills. Online / offline backup Online (the default) backs up while Odoo keeps serving, from one consistent database snapshot. Offline stops Odoo for the backup. Init Job / upgrade Job The Jobs that install modules on a new database (<name>-init) and update them on a new image or token (<name>-upgrade-<hash>). Adopted database A database that existed before the instance pointed at it (status.database.provisionedBy: external). The operator never drops an adopted database. See Databases. Manager The operator's own process, the odoo-operator-controller-manager Deployment.

  • The others count events, each once, on the reconcile that causes it: a Job that stays failed, an image that keeps failing to pull or a drop that keeps failing is not counted again on every requeue. The per-OdooDeployment counters start at 0 and are removed once the OdooDeployment is gone.

(scrape time) odoo_operator_restore_drill_last_success_timestamp_seconds gauge namespace, name When a restore drill of the instance last passed, as a Unix timestamp. Absent until one passes. (scrape time) odoo_operator_restore_last_failed gauge namespace, name 1 when the instance's most recently finished OdooRestore failed. (scrape time) odoo_operator_restores_total counter mode, result In-place restores (OdooRestore) that finished, by mode (restore, undo) and result (succeeded, failed).

docs.title: Operator flags
docs.text:
The manager (odoo-operator, the manager container of odoo-operator-controller-manager) takes these flags. The install bundle sets --metrics-bind-address=:8443, --leader-elect and --health-probe-bind-address=:8081.

Flag Default Effect --metrics-bind-address 0 Where /metrics listens: :8443 for HTTPS, :8080 for HTTP, 0 to turn it off. See Monitoring and alerts. --metrics-secure true Serve metrics over HTTPS, with Kubernetes authentication and authorization. --metrics-secure=false serves plain HTTP. --health-probe-bind-address :8081 Where the liveness and readiness probes listen. --leader-elect false Elect one active manager among the replicas. Only the leader reconciles and reports the scrape-time metrics. --enable-http2 false Allow HTTP/2 on the metrics server; off by default because of the HTTP/2 stream cancellation and rapid reset CVEs. --log-level info debug, info, warn or error. --maintenance-page-image the operator's own image Image of the maintenance page pod. By default the operator reads its own image from its pod. --backup-image the operator's repository with -backup appended, at the same tag Image of the backup, restore, drill and store Jobs. Set it when you mirror images: for example to registry.example.com/odoo-operator-backup:0.6.0.

Mirroring images

An air-gapped or mirrored install needs both images: the operator's and ghcr.io/mohanadabugharbia/odoo-operator-backup at the same tag. When the operator's image is pinned by digest only, the derived backup image falls back to the latest tag; set --backup-image explicitly then.
